top_signal.title: How do you manage your finances as a one-person small business?
top_signal.summary: Hi! I’m a 22-year-old small business owner in the Philippines and I’ve been running my business by myself. I’m basically a one-woman team doing everything from production, purchasing, marketing, admin, finances, packing, etc.   I currently make around ₱40–45k/month in gross sales, with around ₱25k/month in profit.   Over the past 4 months, I’ve managed to save almost ₱80k, but the problem is that I’ve been keeping ALL of my business income in just one personal bank account. 😅 So technically, I don’t really have a proper system for separating business money from my own money.   I want to start doing things properly now and would love advice from other small business owners:   - Should I open a separate bank account specifically for the business?   - How much of my monthly profit should I pay myself as a salary/owner’s draw?   - How much should I keep in the business as working capital?   - How much should I set aside for savings/emergencies and taxes?   - Is it better to give myself a fixed monthly amount or just take money out whenever I need it?   For context, the business is still relatively small, but I’d like to eventually grow it, so I want to build good financial habits now rather than continue mixing everything together.   Would really appreciate any advice or systems that have worked for you! 🙏       submitted by     /u/Technical-Peak-8250       [link]       [comments]
